assets.hypothesis: HIGH DEMAND x THIN ECONOMICS. 2,900/mo and A=74, but F=34 — the model says the leads are too cheap to rent. Tests the new rentability floor itself: can volume compensate for ~$10 per-lead gross profit?
assets.reasonSelected: Selected to test a specific way the A-I model may be WRONG, not because it scores well. Exploration, not exploitation.
assets.falsificationCondition: If it produces many leads that a cleaning company happily pays $300+/mo for, the buckets-1.1.0 economic floor is too strict and is discarding good assets.
assets.scalingCondition: >=$300/mo rent achieved => lower the rentability floor and re-admit high-volume/low-ticket services.
assets.measurementPlan: standard-city-asset + explicit tracking of the dimension under test

assets.hypothesis: V0 SAYS YES, V2 SAYS BARELY. Appliance repair was a V0 favourite; V2 gives it F=34 and nearly always rejects it (1 of 16 bucketed). 1,300/mo with A=67. Tests whether the V0 thesis or the V2 thesis is right about commodity high-volume services.
assets.reasonSelected: Selected to test a specific way the A-I model may be WRONG, not because it scores well. Exploration, not exploitation.
assets.falsificationCondition: If it ranks and rents easily, V2's economic pessimism about commodity services is wrong and D/F need re-calibration.
assets.scalingCondition: rented within 6 months => re-open the fragmented-local service family that V2 currently suppresses.
assets.measurementPlan: standard-city-asset + explicit tracking of the dimension under test

assets.hypothesis: WORST RANKABILITY WE WOULD STILL FUND. A=43 with HIGH-VALUE economics (F=66). Directly tests whether A predicts ranking speed, which is the single most load-bearing assumption in the model.
assets.reasonSelected: Selected to test a specific way the A-I model may be WRONG, not because it scores well. Exploration, not exploitation.
assets.falsificationCondition: If it ranks as fast as the A=75+ assets, A is over-weighted and rankability is not the binding constraint we believe it is.
assets.scalingCondition: top-10 within 6 months => reduce A's weight and admit far more high-economics/hard-SERP markets.
assets.measurementPlan: standard-city-asset + explicit tracking of the dimension under test

assets.hypothesis: MAX RENTER DEPTH x POOR RANKABILITY. E=100 (the strongest renter market found) but A=42. Tests whether renter depth can carry an asset through a hard SERP.
assets.reasonSelected: Selected to test a specific way the A-I model may be WRONG, not because it scores well. Exploration, not exploitation.
assets.falsificationCondition: If it never ranks, E is worthless without A, and renter depth should be demoted to a tie-breaker rather than a 0.17-weight dimension.
assets.scalingCondition: ranks and rents => renter depth deserves more weight relative to rankability.
assets.measurementPlan: standard-city-asset + explicit tracking of the dimension under test
